headline: Sales accelerate, but a tax charge drags earnings down
summary_short: Q2 sales rose 13.6% year over year to $1.74 billion, but net income fell 27.4% to $241.9 million after a $188.2 million tax valuation allowance tied to a California R&D-credit law change.
summary_long: Sales grew 13.6% year over year to $1.74 billion (12.5% constant currency), led by TAVR (+11.3%) and TMTT (+47.3%); Surgical grew 6.5%. Gross margin held flat at 77.5% as FX headwinds offset lower manufacturing costs. Operating margin expanded to 29.5% from 26.8% on operating leverage. GAAP diluted EPS fell 25.0% to $0.42 as a $188.2 million valuation allowance against R&D tax credits (from a California law change) and a $19.9 million impairment charge weighed on the tax rate (53.6% vs 16.1% a year ago); adjusted EPS was $0.78. Cash and short-term investments totaled $4.25 billion. Edwards raised FY2026 sales, TAVR, and TMTT guidance and reaffirmed adjusted EPS guidance of $2.95-$3.05.

drivers.explanation: Growth led by TAVR (SAPIEN durability data, a 2025 competitor exit) and TMTT scaling via PASCAL, EVOQUE, and SAPIEN M3 launches across regions.
R&D fell to 16.0% of sales from 18.0% as revenue outgrew R&D spend, and SG&A leverage improved, expanding operating margin to 29.5%.
A $188.2M valuation allowance from a California R&D tax-credit law change plus a $19.9M VIE impairment pushed the effective tax rate to 53.6% from 16.1%.
EPS decline mirrors the net-income drop from one-off tax and impairment charges; a smaller diluted share count partially offset the impact.
Cash fell versus a year ago on continued share buybacks (about $1.5B of authorization remains) even as short-term investments grew.
CEO Zovighian attributed the quarter to broad-based growth across TAVR, mitral, tricuspid, and surgical platforms with contributions from every region.
